walkthroughs.body_html:
Every magnet has two ends called poles — north and south. 🧲

The rule: like poles repel, unlike poles attract. Two north ends push apart; a north and a south pull together.

This force is non-contact — it works through air and even through paper.

Only some materials feel a magnetic force. The four magnetic materials are iron, steel, cobalt and nickel.

A permanent magnet keeps its magnetism. An induced magnet only acts like a magnet when held near a permanent one — then it lets go.

Steel keeps magnetism well; iron loses it quickly.

A magnetic field is the space around a magnet where another magnet would feel a force.

Field lines go from north to south outside the magnet. Closer lines mean a stronger field.

You can show fields by sprinkling iron filings or by moving a small plotting compass around the magnet.

mcqs.q: Two north poles are brought near each other. What happens?
options: They attract
They repel
Nothing happens
They swap polarity

mcqs.q: Which of these is NOT a magnetic material?
options: Iron
Copper
Cobalt
Nickel

mcqs.q: What produces a magnetic field around a wire?
options: A moving electric charge — i.e. an electric current.
The voltage across the wire creates magnetism.
The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.
The metal in the wire is naturally magnetic.

mcqs.q: If an object is moving at constant velocity in a straight line, what is the net force on it?
options: Zero — by Newton's first law, constant velocity requires zero net force.
The voltage across the wire creates magnetism.
There must be a forward force on the object to keep it moving.
The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.

mcqs.q: A bar magnet has 2 poles. A student joins 6 identical bar magnets end-to-end so each pair sticks at unlike poles. How many free poles remain at the ends of the chain?

numericals.q: A bar magnet has 2 poles. A student joins 6 identical bar magnets end-to-end so each pair sticks at unlike poles. How many free poles remain at the ends of the chain?
numericals.hint: Only the very ends of the chain are free — the inner poles cancel in pairs.

free_texts.q: Field lines around a bar magnet point from one pole to the other (outside the magnet). Which pole do they point AWAY from? Give one word.
free_texts.hint: Lines leave N and enter S.
